title: Albert Grunow diatom collection: sample-level cross-media closure from historical curation instructions
status: S-level historical cross-media addressing architecture; current digital object-level crosswalk still open

primary_sources.source: Schuster et al., An introduction to the catalogue of Albert Grunow's 19th century diatom collection at W including a palaeographic aid, Annalen NHM Wien B 125 (2023), pp. 101-122
Supplementary Information: transcription and images of Grunow's eleven-page curation instructions

sample_cases.maintenance_instruction: If bottled material has dried, Grunow instructs the curator to boil it with nitric acid, remove acid by repeated decantation with distilled water, spread onto cover slips and remount; size fractions could be separated by washing/elutriation.
sample_cases.research_use: Direct sample-level evidence that one number coordinated preserved raw mass and finished glass preparations and also encoded a recipe for recreating usable preparations from deteriorated stored material.

sample_cases.drawing_relation: Grunow explains that a drawing labelled '1363. b (Cagliari) 12.9/32.9' points back to the exact valve on the second preparation of sample 1363.
sample_cases.magnification_relation: The same instructions explain how drawing annotations such as 900/P.O.1 and 1540 magnification record the optical conditions of observation/drawing.
sample_cases.research_use: A single historical sample number crosses locality, preparation identity, slide variant, microscope-stage coordinate and drawing metadata.

Shows the catalogue functioning as a retrievable microscope map: taxonomic observations were stored as coordinates on a named preparation, and a graphical mark recorded whether the located valve had already been drawn.

system_level_findings: Grunow's catalogue is ordered by sample numbers and explicitly distinguishes herbarium material, glass preparations and acid-treated/bottled material.
Multiple glass preparations of one sample can be distinguished by letters and by green strokes in the historical catalogue system.
Older preparations could carry pasted scales; later preparations were localised by aligning the upper-left slide corner to a millimetre scale whose zero coincided with microscope focus.

Drawing sheets retained preparation numbers, valve coordinates, striation measurements and magnification/optical annotations so that published or drawn forms could be returned to the original specimen.

Grunow explicitly instructed successors on rescuing dried bottle material and remaking preparations, so the archive preserves not only addresses but maintenance procedures for reproducing the slide state.
Bottle-material entries whose underline weakened or disappeared could signal that the bottle had been used up, lost its label or been discarded; absence was therefore itself encoded in the catalogue.

upgrade_decision.new: S-level sample-level historical closure for representative sample numbers 274, 1363 and 3073
upgrade_decision.reason: The historical curation instructions provide explicit, sample-numbered crosswalks among stored material, glass preparations, microscope coordinates and drawings rather than merely describing the collection in aggregate.

guard: No current JACQ or NHM persistent record for sample 274, 1363 or 3073 was located in this pass, so the chain currently closes historically rather than through a modern digital object ID.

Sample 274 proves bottle material + glass preparations; sample 1363 proves slide coordinate + drawing; sample 3073 proves coordinate + drawing status. Do not silently merge these into a claim that every individual sample preserves every medium.
Mastogloia Braunii spelling is retained from Grunow's historical instruction; taxonomic modernisation is outside this provenance audit.
next_exact_step: Ask NHM Wien for current collection coordinates or catalogue scans for samples 274, 1363 and 3073, prioritising 1363b and 3073b. A single present-day object record would extend the historical chain into current museum address space.
